answer: Memory-bandwidth challenges force each active bidder to stream a continuous, non-outsourceable hash chain across local RAM during each tide window while a verifier raven audits round-trip latency. Because the raven groups accounts whose latency jitter and egress routes reveal shared physical memory channels, the $j$-th identity bound to the same hardware channel must lock $30j^2$ timber during the tide. A solo newcomer locks 30 timber for one slot, whereas an operator multiplexing $m$ clones on one server must lock $5m(m+1)(2m+1)$ timber or buy $m$ separate physical machines.
